You can see their preliminary numbers here. https://discord.com/channels/890617081744220180/890617129425047583/1349147691522850927 This is early data on use of portal for bulk retrieval of history and worth looking at whether such an approach might serve whatever needs you have at the EL layer. Lets move the history expiry discussion here please, cc <@360491619402776577> <@758579010027782144> <@412614104222531604> <@1009418255913472000> <@687974325072035882> TLDR: - We should do history expiry on sepolia (timeline undecided) - We should use that to then increase gas limit on sepolia - Both things ideally happen before mainnet, so we aren't caught off guard Hey folks! We at Nethermind were looking into history expiry (eip-4444) and how pre-merge history removal might affect CL clients. I want to collect some info on CL teams’ readiness and possible concerns. We did run some preliminary tests (Sepolia, nodes without pre-merge history) to detect calls to `eth_getLogs` and `eth_call` during sync/non-validator node processing. But I was wondering if there are other use cases that we hadn’t considered? yes, that's a very good question, we need to make sure all CL clients are also ready for dropping pre-merge before we do any further increases in the gas limit, I want to see history being dropped first. This means: In order to increase the gas limit on sepolia to 60M, we should be proven that **ALL** EL clients can safely drop pre-merge history on sepolia. I don't care which date its gonna be but doing gas limit increase again before history expiry is done is going backwards. if client teams agree on it being 1st of April, so be it Also going forward in fusaka, I would really like if client teams make gas limit a client parameter that cannot be overriden by users. that way we can much easier schedule a gas limit bump at a fork boundry - reducing gas chaos due to lack of decent testing That's a pretty fundamental change to Ethereum, and would likely see a fair amount of pushback from the community. totally made sense in a PoW world, makes no sense now. Its more of a security issue now imo yeah i think clients making gas limit decisions is a bigger topic that we cant arrive to consensus We need to confirm CL client readiness as well. <@712394671959048244> <@&595683609080365088> <@&595681771690000403> <@&595681804422479873> <@&595683849225240704> Could you check if your client will not query anything from the pre-merge history? but maybe we can scope the discussion here to: - we want to increase gas limit - where can we test it? - what else needs to happen before we increase it? It will be seen as a centralization of power. I won't bother saying any more on this, but don't expect something like that to happen without significant pushback from the community. Core devs should strive to reduce their power over Ethereum, not increase it. I am totally against a hard coded gas limit, without being able to change it for Lodestar this is only the case after Pectra hard fork + deposit transition period is over (~12h) due to changes introduced by EIP-6110 We still have devnets we can test on, but their tx throughput is very low. sepolia is the obvious candidate in terms of "where" for a proper test. So the question seems to be: do we need history expiry before increasing the gas limit on sepolia? On sepolia the four execution nodes I am running (besu, geth, nethermind, reth) are at ~500GB on-disk. If history expiry is purely a case of worrying about diskspace then I don't see an issue with increasing it now, _with the assumption that we will see history expiry on sepolia sometime before 1st May_. If the concern is more around potential time to process blocks with higher gas limits then we should still move ahead with it now, to find out if such concerns are valid or not. Sepolia is a managed validator set, and we can drop the gas limit back down if we see any issues very easily. We can also take a stepped approach (50MM first, then 60MM) if preferred. I'm not sure I understand the argument to drop history before increasing gas limit on sepolia. I see them as two independent features. I think the only reason to link them is on mainnet where disk space is tight for anyone running 2TB. We gotta do it so that we know it works. Otherwise yolo dropping on mainnet without any testing would be pretty nuts. I don’t care if in practice we drop 500GB or 5MB, the fact is that we are doing something new that we haven’t done before. It needs to be tested Agree we should test the history expiry, but I don't think we need to do it before increasing the gas limit (on sepolia) I think we should do it in the same order as we would do on mainnet I see the operational point about doing things in the same order as mainnet, but I don't think there's a technical argument for this. The argument for increasing gas limit sooner on sepolia is we have more time to find and fix issues before users start doing it themselves on mainnet after pectra 🙂 I agree with <@412614104222531604> that we should do the same steps on Sepolia before doing it in mainnet. Otherwise some unknown unknowns could bite us in the arse again Pectra has shown that small differences can lead to big problems I think it's a different class of issues, this isn't a hard fork or likely to cause consensus issues. But hard to argue with unknown unknowns in the current climate 😆 I'm struggling to come to terms with being more yolo about this than <@412614104222531604> ;P I just want to be able to test history expiry before we dig ourself further into the debt of history. excerpts.author: jgm
excerpts.content:
We still have devnets we can test on, but their tx throughput is very low.  sepolia is the obvious candidate in terms of "where" for a proper test.

So the question seems to be: do we need history expiry before increasing the gas limit on sepolia?  On sepolia the four execution nodes I am running (besu, geth, nethermind, reth) are at ~500GB on-disk.  If history expiry is purely a case of worrying about diskspace then I don't see an issue with increasing it now, _with the assumption that we will see history expiry on sepolia sometime before 1st May_.

If the concern is more around potential time to process blocks with higher gas limits then we should still move ahead with it now, to find out if such concerns are valid or not.  Sepolia is a managed validator set, and we can drop the gas limit back down if we see any issues very easily.  We can also take a stepped approach (50MM first, then 60MM) if preferred.
